sections.h2: The two offices behind your bill
sections.html:
Two elected offices share the work. The property appraiser, based at 2001 Adams Lane in Sarasota, determines your parcel's value and who gets an exemption. The tax collector sends out the bill and receives the money. Neither office sets the rate, which each taxing body votes on for itself.

Your real estate notice is one document. It folds ad valorem tax together with non-ad valorem assessments, for example fire protection and solid waste. Business personal property gets its own ad valorem only bill. If nothing arrives by mid-November, contact the collector, who also offers a printable copy online. Counter locations are downtown Sarasota, Venice, North Port and Mid County.

Related pages: Sarasota, North Port and Venice.

Payment opens November 1 and the gross amount is due by March 31. April 1 is when an unpaid balance turns delinquent.

Discounts step down by month: 4 percent for November, 3 for December, 2 for January, 1 for February. Lenders that collect escrow must pay within the 4 percent month. The roll is certified in late September, and bills follow by the end of October.

Two hardship tools exist under state law. Ask the collector for an installment plan by May 1 of the assessment year. A homestead owner may instead file Form DR-570 for a deferral by March 31.

Yearly dates for Sarasota County owners
DateWhat happens
January 1Valuation date and the day exemption eligibility is judged
March 1Last timely day for homestead, senior, disability and nonprofit filings
April 1Tangible personal property returns due; earlier-year tax delinquent
June 1Income papers due for the extra senior exemption
July 1Disapproval notices mailed
Mid-AugustTRIM notices mailed
First week of OctoberCertified roll goes to the collector

You may talk to the appraiser first, but you can also file with the Value Adjustment Board or sue in circuit court without doing so. The three paths need not be taken in order.

A value petition is due 25 days after the TRIM mailing, a date printed on your notice. After a denied exemption or denied assessment transfer you get 30 days from the letter's mailing date. The Clerk to the Value Adjustment Board answers filing questions at (941) 861-5279.

Still unhappy with the board's ruling? A circuit court claim may be filed within 60 days of roll certification. The board looks only at value, classification and exemption. If the rate bothers you, speak up at the budget hearing printed on the notice.

sections.h2: What to bring to a value dispute
sections.html:
Paper beats opinion. Most issues end in informal talks, and what tends to help is proof such as sales comparisons and damage records. Organize it in one folder, with the strongest item on top, and bring two copies so you can leave one behind.

  • Your TRIM notice and parcel number.
  • Closing figures for similar houses sold close by.
  • Contractor estimates or photographs of storm or structural damage.
  • Residency papers if a homestead was denied.

The appraiser's phone is 941.861.8200. Hurricane damage has its own page on the appraiser's site.

sections.h2: From estimate to bill: the yearly calendar
sections.html:
The appraiser's calendar runs from June to the spring after bills go out.

  • By June 1: estimates of taxable value go to each taxing authority.
  • July 1: the appraiser certifies taxable value to each authority.
  • Within 55 days of certification: TRIM notices go out by first class mail.
  • Within 101 days of certification: each authority certifies its final millage to the appraiser and the state revenue department.
  • First week of October: the certified roll is delivered to the collector and the state.
  • March or April: the appraiser tells each authority how Value Adjustment Board decisions and corrections changed the roll.

This sequence explains why a TRIM notice lists proposed rates while the November bill carries final ones. The notice also gives budget hearing dates. Hold on to it until the bill comes, then compare the two side by side.

Homestead leads the list. The house must be your permanent home on January 1, and applications are due March 1. Late filings still get a review.

The exemption is worth up to $50,000, and $25,000 of it reaches school taxes. Afterward the Save Our Homes cap limits yearly growth to 3 percent or CPI, whichever is less. The appraiser's guide adds:

  • $5,000 for a widow or widower who has not remarried.
  • $5,000 for total and permanent disability.
  • $5,000 for blindness.
  • $5,000 for a veteran rated at least 10 percent disabled.
  • For a veteran 65 or older with a permanent combat-related disability, a homestead discount equal to the VA rating percentage.

Voter-approved Amendment 3 reaches the 2027 bill and leaves the 2026 bill as issued.

Tax left unpaid is sold as a certificate, and the holder can eventually ask for a deed. The collector's own wording is blunt: nonpayment can mean losing the property.

Certificates go on sale by June 1. Bidding is on interest, lowest wins, in quarter-point steps. A deed application, carrying a $75 fee, can come two years after the April 1 of the issue year. At the clerk's sale the winner posts a deposit of 5 percent or $200, whichever is more. Our tax deed page goes deeper.

If you're behind, the balance can be paid through closing. Your title agent requests the figure from the collector.

The buyer answers to the collector for the whole bill. Between buyer and seller, the closing statement credits the buyer for the months you held title, and nothing is wired to the collector as a seller part-payment.

Mailing matters afterward. Tell the appraiser where to send your notices once you move, and forward any real estate bill for a house you sold. Business equipment is different: if you owned it on January 1, that year's bill stays yours. Recording details sit in our Sarasota County records guide.

Before listing, pull the parcel record, your last bill and any exemption letters, and ask the collector for a balance that includes older years. Hand the paperwork to the title agent early so questions surface while there is still time to answer them.

On closing day, read the tax proration line on the settlement statement and keep a copy for your records. If a figure looks off, ask the agent to walk you through it before you sign. A cash buyer can close without waiting on a lender, but the same balance check and credit still apply.

After the sale, watch your mail for a few months. Forward any tax notice for the old address to the new owner or the collector, and confirm that the appraiser has the buyer's name on the parcel. Keep the closing papers for your own tax records.

faqs.q: When is Sarasota County property tax due?
faqs.a: Payment opens November 1, and the tax is delinquent after March 31. Early-pay discounts are 4 percent in November, 3 in December, 2 in January and 1 in February.

faqs.q: Where can I pay what I owe?
faqs.a: Use the Sarasota County Tax Collector, through its website payment options or at offices in downtown Sarasota, Venice, North Port or Mid County.
Yes, with a Value Adjustment Board petition filed within 25 days of the TRIM mailing. A denied exemption allows 30 days from the denial letter.

faqs.q: Who pays the tax bill when a house sells?
faqs.a: The buyer answers to the collector. The seller's months are credited to the buyer on the closing statement.

faqs.q: What if I can't pay in full?
faqs.a: Ask the collector about an installment plan, which needs an application by May 1 of the assessment year, or a homestead deferral on Form DR-570 by March 31.
